report.source_text: However, around 3 months later, before her surgery schedule was due, she came to the ED with abdominal pain and tenderness of 12 h duration. She was eventually transferred to the General Surgery Department. Her blood pressure was 150/100 mmHg, heart rate was 110 bpm, respiratory rate was 24×/min, and temperature was 38.3°C. On abdominal examination, there was abdominal tenderness and muscle guarding. No ascites was found. The patient was anemic, with high white blood cell and neutro-phil counts. Other hematological panels were within normal limits. Ultrasonography was performed but there was no free fluid found. Chest X-ray examination revealed bilateral pleural effusions. Perforated appendicitis was suspected and an emergency laparotomy was performed on by the General Surgery Department.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 39-year-old woman presented with an abdominal mass, weight loss, and abnormal uterine bleeding. Initial USG revealed a solid adnexal mass. Three months later, she developed acute abdomen suspected as perforated appendicitis and underwent emergency laparotomy, which revealed a large ruptured cystic mass with solid components adherent to surrounding structures and peritoneal seeding. Intraoperative findings included enlarged uterus and pelvic lymph nodes suspicious for metastases. Histopathology confirmed malignant Brenner tumor of the right ovary infiltrating the corpus uteri, lymphovascular invasion, and metastases to right and left pelvic lymph nodes, rectum, prevesical space, and Douglas pouch.
